headline: Oil-inflation nexus, Iran rejects ceasefire, Houthis hit Saudi tankers — Thursday's -1.2% S&P dip extends. INTC blowout ($16.1B rev, +25% YoY) rescues futures +0.2%. Asia -3% on tech + US 12.5% Japan/Korea tariff shock. Brent settled $100 first time since May.
client_frame: Thursday delivered a textbook multi-front risk event and the tape absorbed it in one go. S&P -1.2% (worst single day in a month), Nasdaq -2.2%, Dow -1%, VIX +12.4% to 18.70 (highest close in six weeks), 10Y to 4.703% (new conflict-period high, up 60bp in a month). Three separate stories converged. First, the Big Tech capex reality-check finished playing through the tape: Alphabet ended the regular session -7.3%, Tesla -8.2%, dragging communication services -5.2% and consumer discretionary -5.1% — those were the two worst S&P 500 sectors of the day. Second, oil went vertical. Brent settled Thursday $100.69, up 7% on the day and above $100 for the first time since May; WTI closed $92.19 (+6.2%). The catalyst was a Houthi claim of strikes on two Saudi tankers in the Red Sea overnight — opening a second chokepoint risk alongside the Strait of Hormuz. WTI is on pace for a 10.9% weekly rise, Brent 13.5%. Third, the diplomatic overlay hardened: Iran rejected the ceasefire proposal delivered by the Iraqi PM overnight; Trump is reportedly weighing what NY Post described as a 'massive attack'; the US House voted a nonbinding war-powers rebuke — the first since the ceasefire breakdown. Overnight, the tape has softened but not broken. Asia was ugly: Nikkei -3.1%, KOSPI -3.7% on a separate US 12.5% tariff announcement on Japan and Korea over forced-labor claims, hitting the Asia tech supply chain (SK Hynix, Samsung -6%). But INTC's after-close report was the surprise of the week and it re-anchored the AI narrative: Q2 revenue $16.13B versus $14.43B consensus (the biggest beat in 15 years, +25% YoY, Data Center segment +59%), Q3 guide well above consensus, and — critically for the capex-panic thesis — Intel is spending, at $20B+ capex, but the return is showing up in the top line right now. Stock touched +13% AH, gave some back to +4-5%. That is the counter-example to GOOGL/TSLA and it is why S&P futures are +0.19% and NQ +0.08% despite the Asia rout. Brent has come off, trading $99.97 in Asia (Reuters), giving some inflation relief. Today's calendar: PMI Flash 9:45 ET (Mfg cons 54.4, Svcs 51.5) — first hard July activity read and it matters into a Wednesday FOMC where cumulative +25bp is now 82% priced. New Home Sales 10:00 (cons 606K SAAR, prior 580K). Fed blackout runs through 7/28. Client framing: the tape is now pricing three-legged risk — AI-capex fatigue on the biggest names, Iranian escalation with a real oil channel, and a hawkish drift in Fed pricing into next week's meeting. INTC re-injects nuance into the capex debate: not every capex-hike is margin destruction; if revenue and mix are ratifying it, the market will pay. Do not chase the futures bounce on INTC alone. Watch three things through the day: (1) does Brent hold below $100 or does another Red Sea headline push it back through — sustained $100 changes the Fed's inflation asymmetry six days from decision; (2) PMI Flash — a print above 55 on Mfg would confirm the growth-inflation stagflation risk the rates market is pricing; (3) does the S&P hold 7,400 — Thursday's low was 7,376, close was 7,408, and 7,400 is where the last-30-day trading range floor sits. Hedges remain paid; keep them on into weekend risk.
